Governments should require large platforms to open their recommendation systems to independent auditors, because self-reporting has repeatedly failed. When Frances Haugen released internal Facebook research in 2021, it showed the company knew Instagram worsened body-image problems for some teenage girls, yet the public learned this only through a leak. Mandatory audits, like the risk assessments required under the EU's Digital Services Act, would surface such findings before a whistleblower has to.

Governments should not force platforms to remove lawful but offensive speech, because the power to define harmful content is easily abused. Germany's NetzDG law, which requires removal of clearly illegal content within 24 hours, has been criticised because platforms facing heavy fines tend to delete borderline posts to be safe. Rules should target transparency and clearly illegal content, not opinions.
